good_when: The maintainers can change what `invoicer` is built with or how it is delivered, such as moving off Python, and the vision still reads true: the `installer`'s role says only what they get done for the `accountant`, `invoicer`'s command set up and running on the `accountant`'s machine, and not which language runtime the command happens to need today.

A maintainer who picks up any planned piece of work, including each idea of the Concept, can tell from the vision the one objective it serves, the accountant's or the installer's, and so knows whose result to check it against. As it stands, two Concept ideas say they serve both O1 and O2, and an accountant who can't print because their machine was never set up right counts as a failure under both KR1.1 and KR2.1.

An accountant reading O1 and KR1.1 knows who 'a developer' is: whether help from the installer, who is also a developer, counts against them, or only help from invoicer's maintainers, so the accounting team and the maintainers count the same invoices as needing a developer's help. The reader also meets one name for the thing that prints the invoice, and never wonders whether 'invoicer' and 'invoicer's command' are two things.
